jobs.occupation: Global Software Sales Manager
jobs.description:
Excited about selling software, being close to customers, and motivated by the next deal?

At AGRAMKOW, we are looking for an experienced Software Sales Manager to grow our software business across the globe. We are looking for someone who combines strong commercial drive with a genuine interest in software, production, and data, and who is motivated by creating business and building strong customer relationships.

About the role

As Software Sales Manager, you will be responsible for driving the growth of our software solutions worldwide.

You will work closely with industrial customers to understand their production environment, data management, integration into ERP and MES systems, identifying where software and data can make a real difference.

The role brings software, products and production data together. You will explore how production data can be generated and used to create greater transparency, insight, and value for our customers, and turn that potential into commercial opportunities.

You will develop business with mainly new potential customers and take commercial ownership of larger and more complex software opportunities across the world.

The position includes frequent travel, bringing you close to customers, their operations, and the environments where our solutions create value.

What you will do

• Drive software sales and business development across the world

• Grow business while actively developing new accounts

• Identify opportunities where software and production data can create measurable customer value

• Understand customers’ production environments, systems, and use of data

• Position our software solutions against customers’ production needs and digitalization ambitions

• Drive and close complex software opportunities

• Build strong relationships with technical, commercial, and senior stakeholders

• Collaborate closely with colleagues across Product, Solutions, Service, and Sales

What we offer

• An important role in developing our software business across the world

• The opportunity to work with software and data in real industrial production environments

• The opportunity to work with complex software sales in an international customer landscape

• A high degree of commercial ownership and direct customer contact

• Access to an established international customer base within manufacturing

• Close collaboration with technical specialists across the organization

• A role at the intersection of software, data, production technology, and sales

• Strong development opportunities within an international organization

About you

You are an experienced Sales Manager or Production Manager with strong commercial drive and an interest in technology, data, and industrial production.

You enjoy being close to customers and are motivated by developing business and closing deals. At the same time, you are technically curious and comfortable engaging in discussions around software, production systems, and data.

You combine technical curiosity with a strong commercial mindset and have the ability to understand complex customer environments without losing sight of the business opportunity.

We imagine that you bring:

• Solid experience with B2B software sales

• A proven track record of closing complex deals

• Experience within industrial software, manufacturing, MES, IoT, automation, production systems, or other data-driven solutions

• Strong commercial drive and experience developing new business

• A strong understanding of, or genuine interest in, how production data can create business value

• Experience with value-based selling

• Experience working across international markets

• Fluent English; additional languages are an advantage

As a person, you are driven, curious, and confident. You build strong customer relationships and are genuinely interested in understanding the business and production environment behind each opportunity.

You work independently and take ownership, while knowing when to bring the right technical expertise into the conversation. You have the commercial ambition and persistence to move opportunities forward and turn them into business.

About AGRAMKOW

AGRAMKOW is a global company delivering technology and solutions to industrial customers worldwide. Our solutions combine equipment, software, data, and services to help manufacturers improve and optimize their production.

You will join an international organization where collaboration, accountability, and continuous development are key to how we work. As our Software Sales Manager, you will have the opportunity to make a real impact on the continued growth of our software business across the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Mathematics - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
This PhD project is part of a new Independent Research Fund project Smooth Tileable Surfaces. Joining the section for Mathematics at DTU Compute, you will help to develop the mathematical theory of a new class of surfaces in geometry, that are characterized as being decomposable into many copies of a small number of so-called prototiles. 

The subject has links to several areas of mathematics, including differential geometry and topology, graph theory and tiling theory, as well as applications in architecture and fabrication. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your focus is to help develop the new subject of smooth tileable surfaces by a) classifying generic subclasses of these surfaces b) establishing an understanding of their relations with graph theory and polyhedral theory, and c) developing methods for geometrically controlled generation of many examples of these surfaces. The overall project also involves collaboration with other team members, working towards the goal of developing not only the mathematical theory of these surfaces, but also algorithms for utilizing them in practical applications in architecture and fabrication.

You must have a background that includes a substantial amount of experience in mathematics, including:

• at least elementary differential geometry, 
• knowledge of, and interest in, some or all of the following subject areas: geometry of surfaces, topology, computational geometry, graph theory, group theory.
A genuine interest in the interplay between theoretical mathematics and applications is also essential.

During the 3 year programme you will:

• Investigate and prove theoretical properties of tileable surfaces
• Develop methods for controlled generation of these surfaces
• Collaborate with other team members on the scientific aspects of the project
• Publish articles in high quality scientific journals
• Present results at scientific conferences
• Contribute to teaching and co-supervision of BsC and MSc students
• Pass approximately 30 ECTS points of relevant coursework
You must have a two-year master's degree in mathematics (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of candidates will be ongoing until the position is filled, and applications received by 15 December are guaranteed full consideration. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk. 

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is 1 March 2027 with some flexibility. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor David Brander by email: dbra@dtu.dk. 

You can read about the project here: https://people.compute.dtu.dk/dbra/TileableProject.html and about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
For full consideration, your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer – (Configuration and programming language design)
jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer – (Configuration and programming language design)

Join Us in Challenging the Life & Pension Sector.

Do you love programming language design, sophisticated verification logic and engineering solutions from start to finish? Festina Finance is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to evolve our configuration solutions, enabling business specialists to define and change the behaviour of the Festina Life and Pension platform.

Our Life & Pension solutions power the biggest pension funds in Denmark and the Netherlands and more than 30 banks across Scandinavia and the UK. As part of our fast‑growing and ambitious organization, you will help shape the core of systems used across Europe while working in a flat, informal culture with plenty of autonomy and room to influence.

What You Will Join

Festina Finance builds modern, high‑performance software platforms for the financial sector. You will join a team of highly skilled developers, actuaries, and domain specialists who work closely together to deliver solutions that are both technically strong and deeply rooted in business logic.

We value craftsmanship, curiosity, and collaboration. You will experience a workplace where people take responsibility, share knowledge, and enjoy solving hard problems together while having fun as a team.

Why this role is exciting

This role gives you the opportunity to work with a highly specialized and industry‑defining product that pushes the boundaries of what is possible in the pension sector. You will operate close to the core of our platform, where programming language design, verification and advanced business logic meet modern software engineering.

The products you will design are at the basis of all calculations and provide the definition of the business in the Festina Life and Pension platform. Scalability, performance, and proper design are key. Here you will get to work in the intersection between programing language design, systems architecture and direct contact with the people who depend on the result. You can expect your solutions to be in use for many years to come.

We produce solutions as a team and frequently have whiteboard sessions discussing upcoming designs and development changes. You can expect to learn through a mixture of individual work and team-based iteration.

What you will work on

Your work will span four main areas:

• Language, semantics and verification: Extend the syntax and semantics of F+, our own in-house functional programming language for financial domains. Design and strengthen the verification logic that ensures configuration is correct before it ever reaches production.

• Systems and architecture: Evolve our purpose-built version control system for F+. You will work with database design, API design, caching strategies, concurrency models, and performance.

• Tooling and operations: Build the configuration tools our business specialists rely on, including applications and integrations, and maintain the CI pipelines and production environment behind them — including monitoring and continuous cluster operations.

• Domain and customers: Analyze business domains, translate them into working solutions, and handle complex customer issues through direct contact with the people using what you build.

Needed skills

To thrive in this role, you should bring strong engineering fundamentals and a mindset suited for mission‑critical systems:

• Strong software engineering fundamentals

• A verification-driven mindset you enjoy building robust validation and verification

• Ability to take an idea from design to implementation while owning responsibility

• Experience designing large‑scale solutions for customers with active production systems

• A highly critical and detail‑oriented mindset our solutions sit at the core of all product calculations

• Strong collaboration skills we communicate intensively when exploring new design spaces

• A master’s degree in computer science or equivalent experience

jobs.occupation: Sr IT and automation engineer
jobs.description:
**Your impact begins here

**As Sr IT and automation engineer, you will keep the systems behind our manufacturing equipment stable, connected and compliant. You will work where automation, IT infrastructure and system validation meet, taking technical responsibility for IT/OT Equipment from design to handover and through its operational life. Your work helps our development pilot plants and production facilities run reliably, so medicines for clinical trials and market supply can reach the people who need them.

**What You’ll Bring

**You do not need to be an expert in every area. Our scope is broad, spanning server infrastructure, automation interfaces, compliance and project delivery. If you have a solid foundation in IT or OT infrastructure, a proactive problem-solving mindset and the curiosity to grow into the rest, we encourage you to apply.

• A relevant degree in Engineering, Automation, Computer Science, IT or a similar technical field, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Solid experience with IT/OT infrastructure and equipment, automation or industrial IT.

• A good understanding of servers, operating systems, networks and industrial connectivity.

• A structured approach to troubleshooting and solving complex technical problems.

• The ability to independently drive technical tasks and deliverables in projects.

• Strong collaboration skills and fluency in English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Experience with SCADA/HMI, PLC communication, OPC UA or industrial Ethernet.

• Experience with GxP, GAMP 5, Data Integrity or system validation.

• Experience with virtualisation, industrial networking, firewall zoning or cybersecurity.

• Experience with PowerShell, Python, Bash or other forms of automation.

• Experience with technical deliverables in engineering or investment projects.

**What You’ll Do

**You will be the technical owner of the IT/OT foundation that manufacturing equipment depends on, handling day-to-day operations and driving projects forward.

• Deploy, configure, patch and maintain servers, Industrial PCs, operating systems and supporting infrastructure, and keep SCADA/HMI platforms and the communication between servers, PLCs and other plant-floor systems running.

• Take technical responsibility for the IT/OT components of manufacturing equipment throughout their lifecycle, planning and executing infrastructure and software upgrades and managing hardware and operating system End-of-Life.

• Drive IT/OT deliverables in equipment and facility projects, from technical scoping and design through commissioning and handover.

• Drive technical validation activities, keep Computerised Equipment in a validated state, maintain lifecycle documentation and support change controls in line with GxP and Data Integrity requirements.

• Perform technical IT Risk Assessments and support patching, access management, firewall reviews and network segmentation.

• Lead technical investigations and recovery of complex IT/OT incidents, infrastructure failures and communication issues, take part in the rotating on-call scheme for critical manufacturing infrastructure, and use scripting, automation and AI-assisted tools to simplify recurring tasks.

**Who You’ll Work With

**In Chemistry, Manufacturing & Control (CMC), we translate groundbreaking research into medicines for clinical trials and market supply worldwide. You will join CMC IT Operations & Digitalisation, part of Global Manufacturing & Supply, where we provide the reliable, compliant and secure IT/OT foundation for IT/OT Equipment across our development pilot plants and production facilities.

Day to day, you will work closely with automation engineers, equipment owners, project managers and central IT functions. You will also support international projects and sister sites in the Czech Republic and the US, so you can expect 10–20 days of travel per year. Clear priorities and honest, timely communication between these groups help you resolve issues quickly and keep projects moving.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will be trusted to work independently and take ownership of your technical area, with colleagues who value practical engineering curiosity as much as experience. The role spans operations, validation, cybersecurity and projects, giving you room to build new skills across the value chain and grow with your colleagues on the job. You will also be encouraged to use AI-assisted tools to improve how the work gets done.

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000 DKK – 956,900 DKK (DK), corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy **here

****Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to keep critical manufacturing systems stable, compliant and moving forward, apply for the Senior IT/OT Operations Professional role by 1st December 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Hiring Manager Asger Cederberg at **OYHA@novonordisk.com

jobs.occupation: 14 postdoctoral fellowships to the BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme
jobs.description:
BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme
 The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme at the University of Copenhagen is seeking 14 highly motivated and dynamic postdoc fellows to commence the BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme on 1 September 2027.

  The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation with the ambition to train fellows in translational medicine, mentored by fully committed and top-level professionals in basic biomedical research, a clinical environment and the life science industry. The programme constitutes a clear career path for candidates whose ambition is to bridge the gap between research, patient care and the life science industry and for those wishing to become pioneering leaders in the field of translational medicine.

  The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme expects to appoint 7 fellows with an MD background and 7 fellows with an MSc background. The fellow will be appointed in the lab of the basic mentor either at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND) or the Faculty of SCIENCE (SCIENCE), UCPH.

  Application deadline is 9 February 2027, at 23:59 CET. Appointed fellows are expected to participate in a two-day Boot Camp on 9-10 September 2027. Mentors are expected to participate on 9 September 2027.

  Translational research project
 Your research project must cover the early translational stages T₀ (Disease modelling, Omics studies, Basic Research) -T₁ (Biomarker discovery, Target development, Preclinical development) and should bridge a basic biomedical research environment and a clinical research environment, making the research project interdisciplinary in its nature. The project may also cover early T₂ (First in human, phase 1 clinical trials, phase 2 clinical trials, phase 2b clinical trials), but this is not a requirement. 

  Your project must be at the postdoctoral level, should address a relevant medical challenge and should be ambitious yet feasible within the timeframe of two years. Your research project must be developed in collaboration with your Mentor Team and is an important part of the recruitment process to become a BRIDGE Fellow.

  Appointed fellows spend 80% of their time on individual translational research projects mentored by a Mentor Team consisting of a basic biomedical scientist from a SUND or SCIENCE Department or Centre, and a clinical scientist from a hospital in the Capital Region of Denmark or Region Zealand and/or from the life science industry. Additional mentors from other departments and universities in Denmark are encouraged if relevant.

  Academic Curriculum
 The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme provides fellows with the ability to translate insights from basic research into the clinical sciences and/or the life science industry, and vice versa, and the competences to manage essential collaboration between disciplines.

  A uniquely developed 55 days Academic Curriculum has been designed by top-professional experts and figures as a mandatory, integral, and important part of the BRIDGE programme. 

  The Academic Curriculum covers the translational stages T₀ (Population/clinic to lab feedback, disease modelling -omic studies, basic research), T₁ (Biomarker discovery, target development, pre-clinical development) and border to early T₂ (First in human, phase 1 clinical trials, phase 2 clinical trials, phase 2b clinical trials). 

  In addition, courses also include generic skills such as research management, ethics, research communication and successful grant writing. The Academic Curriculum and additional events such as the Boot Camp, Academic Afternoons, Alumni Event comprise 20% of fellows’ time. The fellows should therefore not be imposed teaching obligations during their fellowship.

  Eligibility
 Future BRIDGE Fellows must hold one of the following: 

   	
• An MD and a PhD degree or equivalent (proof of an appointment that requires doctoral equivalency). Specialist training is no hindrance to apply, and medical training is appreciated.    	
• An MSc and a PhD degree or equivalent (BSc integrated PhD) within a relevant discipline such as veterinary science, biology, biochemistry, molecular biology, bioinformatics, pharmacy, dentistry, or medical engineering.   The following requirements must also be met:

  The PhD degree should have been obtained no more than eight years before the application deadline. Any documented periods of leave will be accepted as extensions of this time limit (maternity leave, paternity leave, family care leave, illness, military service, etc.).

  As a current PhD student, you may apply if you and your supervisor expect your thesis to be submitted and defended prior to project commencement on 1 September 2027.  You must attach a declaration from your supervisor stating that your thesis will be submitted and defended prior to project commencement on 1 September 2027.

  In Denmark, you can hold postdoc positions for no more than a total of four years at one university. Accordingly, no more than two years of postdoc experience based at one of the departments at UCPH prior to programme enrolment is allowed. Any documented periods of leave will be accepted as extensions of this time limit (parental leave, family care leave, illness, military service, etc.). Please find more information about the 'four-year rule' for postdocs (Danish legislation) under 'Eligibility and conditions' and about the applicable governmental jurisdiction here.

  Mentor Teams
 The applicant must apply for the programme in cooperation with a Mentor Team consisting of a minimum of two mentors.

  A Mentor Team requires a mentor representing 1) the basic biomedical science from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND) or the Faculty of SCIENCE (SCIENCE), UCPH, and 2) clinical science from the Capital Region of Denmark or Region Zealand and/or 3) the life science industry environment in Denmark. A life science industry mentor is highly encouraged to enter the Mentor Team.

  We also encourage larger mentor teams with additional mentors from Technical University of Denmark (DTU), or other universities or research institutions, if relevant. 

  Incorporating a mentor from SUND or SCIENCE, UCPH, into the Mentor Team is mandatory. If a mentor acts as a third, fourth or fifth mentor – accompanying a basic and clinical mentor – that mentor may reside outside Denmark.

  NOTE: One can only be a mentor for maximum two candidates for each call. 

  Qualifications
 As a BRIDGE fellow, you are highly motivated to participate in the Academic Curriculum, to be mentored by senior researchers, network and cooperate with other BRIDGE Fellows and you see yourself as an ambitious scientist who will work on bridging the gaps between research, medical treatment and/or the life science industry.

  We expect BRIDGE Fellows to be scientifically independent, showing a high degree of academic maturity. This means that they will have:

   	
• An enthusiastic interest in a translational research project co-designed with a Mentor Team and be a good match with a committed Mentor Team 	
• A strong CV, having published peer reviewed original manuscripts in high-quality journals with minimum one first author paper and presented at international conferences 	
• The ability to manage one’s own academic research and associated activities 	
• Experience with project management 	
• Experience with research supervision of more junior researchers (pre-graduate or PhD students) or clinicians  	
• Excellent interpersonal skills and leadership, including the ability to communicate research ideas and results in a clear and logical way and the ability to interact with peers and the broader research community confidently and effectively   How to apply
 As a BRIDGE fellow, you will be working on a translational research project co-designed with a Mentor Team. As such, the first step in the application process is to connect with a Mentor Team.

  If you are not already in contact with an eligible Mentor Team, we recommend that you:

   	
• Contact a (i) basic biomedical researcher from SUND or SCIENCE, UCPH, a (ii) clinical scientist from a hospital in the Capital Region of Denmark or Region Zealand and/or (ii) a scientist from the life science industry who fits your research interests and fulfil the programme requirements for Mentor Teams. We recommend that you have the Mentor Team preapproved in due time before application deadline 9 February 2027 by sending a request to BRIDGE: bridge@sund.ku.dk 	
• Alternatively, browse through the list of submitted project synopses (Open Mentor Teams) and find a Mentor Team that fits your research interests. Contact the suitable Mentor Team to explore the possibility of collaborating on a BRIDGE application. The list will be published on the BRIDGE website on 14 December 2026.   If you are an applicant without ties to the Faculty or hospitals in either of the two regions, please read more about our suggestions on how to proceed here.

  If you are in contact with a Mentor Team, we recommend that you:

   	
• Have the Mentor Team constellation preapproved in due time before the call closure by sending a request to BRIDGE: bridge@sund.ku.dk.   Read more about how to become a fellow.

   Application material

   	
• Part 1: Project description (must be co-designed by the applicant and Mentor Team) 	
• Part 2: Project abstract and CV (must be composed by the applicant independently) 	
• Part 3: Supplementary documents    Applications (Part 1, Part 2, and Part 3) must be submitted online through the link on the website no later than 9 February 2027, 23:59 CET. A cover letter is not needed, and there is no need for entering the application in NORMA. 

  Please find the requirements for the application and download the new and updated application templates.

  We reserve the right to disregard material received after the application deadline along with applications and application material that do not comply with the above-mentioned criteria. 

  Recruitment procedure  
 The received applications will be shortlisted and assessed according to the Ministry Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities 2012 and the University of Copenhagen’s guidelines 2013.  

  Upon the application deadline, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the Appointment Committee.

  All applicants will be notified on whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Assessment Committee will do a non-prioritised assessment based on the applicant’s academic qualifications and on the match between the fellow and the translational research project. All applicants will have the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves (Part 2).

  Please find more information on the recruitment process for scientific personnel at the University of Copenhagen.

  Appointment interviews
 Following the completion of the assessments, a subset of candidates will be invited for a physical appointment interview with the Appointment Committee. The BRIDGE Programme will reimburse travel and accommodation expenses for invited applicants.

  The interviews are scheduled to take place 11-13 May 2027. Please note that Mentor Teams will need to be present online for a short introduction of the Mentor Team at this interview.

  Terms of employment
 The employment as Postdoc is fulltime (37 hours per week) and for two years. The start date is on 1 September 2027.

  Salary, pension, and terms of employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) and the Ministry of Finance. 

  The position is covered by the “Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at the Universities” of 2025.

  Financial composition of the fellowships
 The financing of running costs for the individual research projects will be covered by the hosting environments. Each fellow will in addition receive an annual sum of DKK 40,000 during their two-year employment to cover costs for PC, travel, language courses, conference and workshop participation and other relevant activities outside the programme.

  Successful fellowship recipients will be enrolled in the BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme and employed at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at UCPH. Upon fulfilment of course participation and the individual research projects, fellows will be awarded a Certificate of Excellence.

  For more information about the BRIDGE - Translational Excellence Programme  
 Please visit www.bridge.ku.dk and/or contact Programme Manager Kathrine Bjerregaard Nielsen on bridge@sund.ku.dk or telephone +45 35 32 98 71.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Do you want to help develop novel instrumentation for groundwater investigations? At the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aarhus University, we are seeking a motivated postdoctoral researcher in electrical engineering to contribute to the development of novel nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) instruments for groundwater characterization. You will join an interdisciplinary research environment spanning electrical engineering, geophysics, and environmental science working on technologies that can improve our understanding of vital groundwater resources. The 2-year position is based in Aarhus, Denmark and is available from 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from 1 March 2027 or as soon possible thereafter.

We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher in electrical engineering to help develop a new generation of surface NMR instruments for groundwater characterization. Through a recently funded research project, we are building a new instrument with capabilities beyond those of existing systems. As part of the project, you will play a central role in designing and integrating key electronic subsystems and in exploring how the resulting instrument can open new possibilities for groundwater investigations.

Your tasks will include

• Design, simulation, construction, and validation of electronic subsystems
• Interfacing of ADCs and DACs to analog frontends and a microcontroller
• Integration of subsystems into a complete instrument
• Experimental work, including testing of instruments and data collection in both laboratory and field environments
• Data analysis
• Co-supervision of bachelor and master thesis projects within the project
• Documentation of technical development and research results
• Leading and contributing to scientific publications
You will join a collaborative and interdisciplinary team where you will be working closely with other researchers, technicians, and students at the Department. The project also involves interaction with researchers and end-users working directly with groundwater characterization.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in electrical engineering or similar. 

Prior experience with surface NMR or groundwater measurements is not required, but we expect you to a have a curiosity for these areas.

We are looking for candidates with experience in several of the following areas:

• Electronic systems design
• Development of low-noise analog and digital electronics including power supplies
• Interfacing to/from ADCs and DACs
• PCB layout
• Solving EMC issues
• Practical electronic and laboratory skills
• Data analysis
Experience in one or more of the following areas is considered advantageous:

• Real-time data acquisition systems implemented on microcontrollers
• Embedded Linux
• Power electronics
• Signal processing and embedded signal processing
It is also advantageous if you have a driver’s license.

Personal skills
You have good English skills, both in speaking and in writing. You take responsibility for assigned tasks and communicate openly about progress, challenges, and ideas. You can work independently as well as in a team. You are open-minded, curious, and have a good sense of humour. We value the ability to work independently as well as in a team.

The project will focus on developing automated approaches for feature extraction, annotation, and interpretation of non-target data, with a particular focus on automatically tracking and identifying previously unknown parent compounds and their likely transformation products as indicators of chemical reaction pathways in technical processes, including classical and advanced wastewater treatment. The resulting approaches will contribute to improved environmental monitoring, assessment of wastewater treatment performance, and the identification of emerging contaminants relevant to chemical risk assessment.

We're looking for a Market Procurement Manager, Indirects to strengthen procurement capability, governance and value creation across Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

About Royal Unibrew

Royal Unibrew is a leading multi-beverage company operating across the Nordics, Baltics and selected international markets. With a portfolio that includes well-known brands such as Faxe Kondi, Booster, Egekilde, Royal, Ceres, Albani and Faxe, we are committed to being the preferred local beverage partner while continuously driving growth, innovation and sustainability.

Today, Royal Unibrew employs thousands of colleagues across multiple countries and continues to invest in both people and capabilities that support long-term success.

The Role

We're looking for an experienced procurement professional who thrives on creating structure, driving improvements and influencing stakeholders in a dynamic business environment.

As Market Procurement Manager, Indirects, you will be responsible for developing and executing procurement strategies across a broad portfolio of indirect spend categories, including:

• Marketing Services

• Professional Services

• Maintenance, Repair & Operations (MRO)

• Other local indirect spend categories

This is not a role focused solely on managing established categories. A significant part of your success will come from identifying opportunities, building procurement maturity, implementing governance frameworks, improving spend visibility and helping stakeholders make commercially sound decisions.

You will work closely with stakeholders across Denmark, Norway and Sweden while collaborating with suppliers, internal business functions and Group Procurement colleagues to drive value creation and support Royal Unibrew's continued growth ambitions.

• Develop and implement procurement and category plans across multiple indirect spend categories

• Lead sourcing initiatives, supplier tenders and commercial negotiations

• Build and strengthen procurement governance, sourcing frameworks and best practices

• Increase transparency, control and visibility across indirect spend

• Establish and drive supplier relationship and performance management activities

• Identify and deliver cost optimization and value creation opportunities

• Support demand management and compliance initiatives

• Influence stakeholders and challenge existing ways of working constructively

• Analyse spend data, supplier performance and market developments

• Contribute to procurement capability development across Denmark, Norway and Sweden

• Strong stakeholder management and business partnering capabilities

• Experience driving governance, compliance and process improvements

• Experience operating in a complex stakeholder environment with multiple priorities

• Experience from FMCG, consumer goods, retail, manufacturing or other stakeholder-intensive environments

• Commercially minded and business-oriented

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity and creating structure where needed

• Proactive, hands-on and self-driven

• Resilient and confident when challenging stakeholders constructively

• Curious, improvement-focused and eager to drive change

• Skilled at influencing without direct authority

• Motivated by ownership, accountability and visible business impact

Joining Royal Unibrew means becoming part of a company with strong local brands, ambitious growth plans and a culture built on entrepreneurship, ownership and collaboration.

You will have the opportunity to:

• Shape procurement maturity and ways of working across multiple markets

• Take ownership of a broad indirect spend portfolio spanning several business-critical categories

• Microbial Foods
• Sustainable Food Innovation
• Fermentation Cultures

You will use your scientific expertise and experience to strengthen the quality, reproducibility, and efficiency of research activities, while helping to ensure that researchers have access to the infrastructure, biological resources, methodologies, and support needed to conduct research at an international level.

The position combines scientific support, infrastructure development, coordination, and laboratory management. You will be expected to work independently and apply sound academic judgement in a broad range of situations, ranging from the development of research workflows and management of biological resources to advising researchers on laboratory practices, documentation standards, and implementation of new methodologies.

A central part of the position will be the continued development and stewardship of shared biological and laboratory resources. You will contribute to the development of standards and practices that can be applied across multiple research projects and research groups.

What we offer in return
We offer a dynamic, versatile, and highly enthusiastic research environment at the forefront of food innovation, microbiology, sustainability science, and human health. You will gain unique insight into cutting-edge research taking place across multiple interdisciplinary groups, all working towards solutions for the green transition.

The role provides a central and highly trusted position within the research infrastructure, giving you significant responsibility and ownership over the daily functioning and long-term organization of shared laboratory facilities. You will work closely with researchers at all levels—from students to senior scientists—and become a key link across multiple projects and disciplines.

You will be part of a welcoming, collaborative, and international working environment with strong scientific ambition and a clear focus on real-world impact. The position offers extensive exposure to advanced laboratory workflows, state-of-the-art infrastructure, and best practices in laboratory management, quality control, and scientific data organization.

Beyond day-to-day operations, this role provides an excellent opportunity to develop professionally in areas such as academic research, laboratory coordination, research support strategy, compliance, and scientific infrastructure management, while contributing directly to high-impact research in sustainable food systems.

Salary and appointment terms

In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

BRIGHT Mission 2 aims to build an AI-powered framework for the rational design of microbial foods that meet four targets: consumer acceptance, health, sustainability and scalability. The first phase focuses on two fungal chassis, Aspergillus and Yarrowia, characterizing more than 500 prototypes through multi-omics, sensory analysis, life-cycle assessment and safety testing. Predictive models for flavor, texture, nutrition and process scale-up are trained iteratively through active learning. The scientific scope spans strain engineering, adaptive laboratory evolution, solid- and liquid-state fermentation, sensory and consumer research, and pre-clinical and clinical evaluation of safety, bioavailability and cardiometabolic health, in collaboration with national and international partners.

jobs.description:
The Platform Tribe is undergoing a significant transformation, moving away from a centralized enterprise data warehouse to an approach that supports domain-oriented decentralized data ownership. Domains are empowered to own their data with a product mindset. They focus on delivering clear value and ensuring high quality. These domains publish data products supported by self-serve data infrastructure as a platform, underpinned by federated computational governance. This governance promotes collaboration, establishes shared standards, and enforces automated policies.

As a new Senior Data Architect, you will join the Data Platform Tribe, which is operationally responsible for systems within Data & Analytics. The Tribe consists of 150 team members across Denmark, Lithuania, and India.

The Senior Data Architect role involves designing solutions that meet business and development requirements while aligning with strategic architecture direction and roadmaps. A core aspect of your responsibilities will be shaping and advancing standards and governance policies to guide data ingestion, technical design and development of data products, publishing in the data marketplace, and the implementation of robust data quality frameworks within a data mesh environment. Additionally, the role requires maintaining advanced knowledge across multiple technologies, domains, and disciplines, including event-driven data architectures, data management frameworks such as DMBOK, semantic web concepts, and linked data principles.
